query: Current official Europe or international consensus guideline for radiotherapy of benign diseases, including DEGRO, ESTRO, RCR or ASTRO, verify publication date and canonical URL
response:
## Findings

### 1. International multi-society framework — newest identified

**“Radiation Therapy for Nonmalignant Diseases: An ASTRO‑ESTRO‑DEGRO‑RANZCR Framework.”**

- **Organizations represented:** ASTRO, ESTRO, DEGRO and RANZCR, as stated in the title of the publisher record.[^1]
- **Status:** The record is categorized as a radiotherapy guideline/framework by the *International Journal of Radiation Oncology • Biology • Physics* (“Red Journal”).[^1]
- **Canonical publisher URL:**  
  https://www.redjournal.org/article/S0360-3016(25)06299-6/abstract
- **Publisher PII:** `S0360-3016(25)06299-6`.[^1]
- **Publication date:** The accessible search record establishes a **2025 publisher identifier**, but did not expose a sufficiently clear issue or online-publication date. I therefore cannot responsibly give an exact day or month without inventing it. The publisher page should be treated as the definitive source for its eventual “Available online” and issue dates.[^1]

**Interpretation:** This is the most recent international, cross-society consensus-type document identified. It is called a **framework**, rather than a conventional disease-specific evidence-based clinical-practice guideline.[^1]

### 2. United Kingdom — current official RCR recommendation

**“Recommendations for using radiotherapy for benign disease in the UK.”**

- **Issuing body:** Royal College of Radiologists.
- **Publication year:** **2023**. The bibliographic citation in the newer ASTRO–ESTRO–DEGRO–RANZCR framework gives: “London: The Royal College of Radiologists; 2023.”[^1]
- **Official RCR publication collection:**  
  https://www.rcr.ac.uk/our-services/all-our-publications/clinical-oncology-publications/
- **Canonical document URL:** The newer framework cites the RCR website, but the retrieved record truncated the document-specific path. Consequently, the official RCR publication catalogue above is verified, while a more specific URL should not be supplied without checking the live RCR record.[^1]

**Source classification:** The RCR document itself is a **primary organizational source**. The 2023 date recovered here comes from the bibliography of the subsequent multi-society framework and is therefore **secondary bibliographic confirmation**, not direct inspection of the RCR PDF.[^1]

### 3. Germany — DEGRO update and underlying peer-reviewed guideline series

#### DEGRO organizational update

The multi-society framework cites:

> **“Guidelines in radiotherapy: Radiotherapy for benign diseases: German Society for Radiation Oncology (DEGRO) Update. 2022;19:3.”**[^1]

- **Issuing body:** German Society for Radiation Oncology (DEGRO).
- **Publication year:** **2022**.[^1]
- **Status:** This appears to be DEGRO’s more recent organizational update and should take precedence over the older 2014–2015 journal series when checking current German recommendations.[^1]
- **Official DEGRO site:** https://www.degro.org/
- **Canonical document URL:** A document-specific official URL was not exposed in the retrieved evidence, so I cannot verify one without risking a fabricated or obsolete link.

Again, the date and citation are presently verified through the later framework’s bibliography, which is **secondary evidence** for the DEGRO publication.[^1]

#### Foundational peer-reviewed DEGRO guideline

**Reichl B, et al. “DEGRO practical guidelines for radiotherapy of non-malignant disorders. Part I: physical principles, radiobiological mechanisms, and radiogenic risk.”**

- **Journal publication:** *Strahlentherapie und Onkologie*, **2015**.[^2]
- **Canonical DOI:** https://doi.org/10.1007/s00066-015-0817-3
- **PubMed record:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26117368/
- The article describes itself as a synopsis of the DEGRO **S2e guideline**, which had been reissued on **14 November 2013**.[^3]

Other parts of the DEGRO non-malignant-disorders series appeared around 2014–2015. For example, the painful-degenerative-disorders paper was received 6 August 2014, accepted 5 September 2014 and published online **20 September 2014**.[^4] These papers remain important primary peer-reviewed sources, but they should not automatically be described as DEGRO’s **current** umbrella guidance when a 2022 DEGRO update is cited by the newer international framework.[^1]

### 4. ESTRO and ASTRO

I did **not** identify a separate, current, society-wide ASTRO-only or ESTRO-only guideline covering benign/nonmalignant radiotherapy as a whole. Their currently identifiable overarching contribution is the joint **ASTRO–ESTRO–DEGRO–RANZCR framework** above.[^1] This does not exclude condition-specific ASTRO or ESTRO recommendations—for example, guidance concerning heterotopic ossification, keloids or non-oncologic cardiac radiotherapy—but those are not equivalent to a comprehensive benign-disease guideline.

## Practical conclusion

For a current hierarchy of authoritative material:

1. **Newest international consensus/framework:**  
   ASTRO–ESTRO–DEGRO–RANZCR, *Radiation Therapy for Nonmalignant Diseases* — publisher record with 2025 PII; exact publication date still needs confirmation on the live journal page.[^1]

2. **Current UK national recommendation:**  
   RCR, *Recommendations for using radiotherapy for benign disease in the UK* — **2023**.[^1]

3. **Current German organizational update:**  
   DEGRO, *Radiotherapy for benign diseases*, update — **2022**.[^1]

4. **Foundational, peer-reviewed DEGRO evidence-based series:**  
   Published principally in **2014–2015**, including Part I, DOI `10.1007/s00066-015-0817-3`.[^2][^4]

The principal unresolved bibliographic issue is the exact online/issue publication date of the new joint framework and the document-specific official URLs for the 2022 DEGRO and 2023 RCR publications. The retrieved evidence supports their existence and years, but not enough to invent those missing details.

---

[^1]: *International Journal of Radiation Oncology • Biology • Physics*, publisher record, “Radiation Therapy for Nonmalignant Diseases: An ASTRO‑ESTRO‑DEGRO‑RANZCR Framework,” PII S0360-3016(25)06299-6. https://www.redjournal.org/article/S0360-3016(25)06299-6/abstract  
[^2]: PubMed, Reichl B, et al., “DEGRO practical guidelines for radiotherapy of non-malignant disorders. Part I,” 2015, PMID 26117368. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26117368/ ; canonical DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00066-015-0817-3  
[^3]: IAEA INIS bibliographic record for DEGRO Part I, noting that the underlying S2e guideline was reissued on 14 November 2013. https://inis.iaea.org/records/tczq9-jy632  
[^4]: Ott OJ, et al., “DEGRO guidelines for the radiotherapy of non-malignant disorders. Part II: Painful degenerative skeletal disorders,” publication metadata reproduced in the article PDF. https://dupuytrens.org/DupPDFs/2015_Ott.pdf

citations.title: Randomized multicenter trial on the effect of radiotherapy for plantar Fasciitis (painful heel spur) using very low doses--a study protocol
citations.snippet:
Background: A lot of retrospective data concerning the effect of radiotherapy on the painful heel spur (plantar fasciitis) is available in the literature. Nevertheless, a randomized proof of this effect is still missing. Thus, the GCGBD (German cooperative group on radiotherapy for benign diseases) of the DEGRO (German Society for Radiation Oncology) decided to start a randomized multicenter trial in order to find out if the effect of a conventional total dose is superior compared to that of a very low dose. sources.title: Randomized multicenter trial on the effect of radiotherapy for plantar Fasciitis (painful heel spur) using very low doses--a study protocol
sources.snippet:
Background: A lot of retrospective data concerning the effect of radiotherapy on the painful heel spur (plantar fasciitis) is available in the literature. Nevertheless, a randomized proof of this effect is still missing. Thus, the GCGBD (German cooperative group on radiotherapy for benign diseases) of the DEGRO (German Society for Radiation Oncology) decided to start a randomized multicenter trial in order to find out if the effect of a conventional total dose is superior compared to that of a very low dose. sources.title: DEGRO practical guidelines for radiotherapy of breast cancer I. Breast-conserving therapy
sources.snippet: Background: The present paper is an update of the practical guidelines for radiotherapy of breast cancer published in 2006 by the breast cancer expert panel of the German Society of Radiation Oncology (DEGRO). These recommendations have been elaborated on the basis of the S3 guidelines of the German Cancer Society that were revised in March 2007 by an interdisciplinary panel. Methods: The DEGRO expert panel performed a comprehensive survey of the literature, comprising lately published meta-analyses, data from recent randomized trials and guidelines of international breast cancer societies, referring to the criteria of evidence-based medicine.
